reviewer_text: New applications install the packages each decision names plus scaffold packages: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design where migrations are created, a Console sink for local logging, NUnit3TestAdapter and Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk in test projects (reported as fixed packages beyond the concrete-need rule).

The local connection-string example trusts the server certificate, while the prose forbids committing any usernames, passwords, tokens, production hosts or production connection strings (reported: broader than real secret credentials).

A project-reference change outside the accepted graph is Reserved: raise a Decision Request and, after approval, run the reference command with the trailing comment '# project-references: approved' (reported: even legal internal references need a literal approval marker).
Every security report states that the scan is an evidence-based static review, not a penetration test, and cannot prove the application secure (reported as required even for a narrow verified issue).
No generated or build artifacts were added to the change (reported as barring intentionally maintained generated source, broader than removing accidental artifacts).
Small solutions run the complete test suite; large solutions run affected test projects first, then the broader suite the risk requires (reported as regardless of scope and risk).
Report what was actually run with PASS, FAIL, NOT RUN or NOT APPLICABLE; the example matrix omits FAIL/NOT RUN for some areas (reported risk of incomplete skipped-check reports).
Application services, repositories and external adapters use interface-to-implementation registration at architectural boundaries; implementation-only helpers can be registered concretely.
Load the knowledge skill for each technology involved (reported as required regardless of relevance).

The development-workflow output states what changed and why, Delegated decisions taken, Decision Requests raised or still unresolved, and the verification report (reported as requiring enumeration of Delegated decisions).
Keep build tooling out of production runtime images (reported as broader than avoiding SDK images for convenience).
Configure the Testing environment with isolated test resources so an integration test cannot reach a development or production database by accident (reported: the environment name is prescribed).
Keep slow or unreliable external-system tests separate from ordinary fast runs (reported as regardless of existing suite design).
Keep entity configuration in IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> classes (reported as prescribed beyond confining persistence configuration to Infrastructure).
Paginate in the database with deterministic ordering; the example orders only by CreatedAt (reported: equal timestamps are not uniquely ordered).

Detect existing data with representative root/anchor entities; the seeder assumes the schema is already migrated; for a new local database apply migrations first, then startup seeds the empty schema (reported: the detection method and startup trigger are prescribed).
Raw SQL fits queries EF Core cannot express effectively or a measured performance need (reported as narrower than a measured or clearly demonstrated need).

Additional status mappings: 406/415 for negotiation and media types, 409, 412, 422, 428, 429 with Retry-After when known, 500, 502, 503 with Retry-After when meaningful, and 504, each with stated limits.
When HTTP optimistic concurrency is part of the contract use standard conditional requests (ETag/If-Match) instead of custom status codes.
The Microsoft resilience packages build on Polly v8, but application code uses the Microsoft.Extensions resilience APIs (reported as omitting the direct-Polly exception).
The Serilog bootstrap example logs a fatal startup failure without rethrowing or setting a failure exit code (reported failure-visibility uncertainty).
Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch is deprecated; use Elastic.Serilog.Sinks (reported: a fixed replacement and log-storage defaults may be acted on beyond version-specific due diligence).
The C# property example trims and rejects blank names silently (reported copy risk for unapproved string semantics).
Api Controllers are thin ASP.NET Core Controllers; no Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested (reported as stricter than Controllers merely being the default).

The add-dependency output reports package, selected version and why, license, deprecation and vulnerability status, approval obtained, files changed and the verification result (reported as a fixed field set).
Use computed for derived state and avoid effect() when computed, template binding or explicit event handling expresses the dependency more clearly.
The error-handling example maps request cancellation to status 499 (reported as a status choice beyond the cancellation rule).

Stop and reassess when the same root failure survives different fixes, fixes create growing failures, toolchain or infrastructure is unavailable, compatibility cannot be resolved safely or correct behavior cannot be determined (reported: may halt independent source repair that is still possible).
Measure before adding caching purely for performance (reported as requiring measurement where a measured or reasoned need suffices).
The output-cache example embeds a five-minute TTL without a local illustrative-value caveat (reported copy risk).

Identify the changed behavior, error cases, effects and tests; read the standards for touched scopes and load the knowledge skill for each changed technology area (reported as required regardless of sufficient context).

Severity definitions: Critical (data loss, security vulnerability, reliably broken core behavior; blocks use or merge immediately), High (likely defect or architecture/data-integrity issue; fix before merge), Medium (real maintainability, robustness or test gap), Low (non-blocking improvement).

Product inputs may request a decision change but never silently override CLAUDE.md, the register or a standard; a deviation from a default needs a concrete reason and must be reported (reported: may constrain otherwise authorized specification choices).
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict; on conflict stop and ask which source must be corrected (reported as excluding resolution of an obviously stale source).

Decisions are classified Decided/Delegated/Reserved; the unclear-case test reserves any dependency addition/removal and any convention or reference change, and accepted decisions follow fixed reporting and recording procedures (reported tension with Delegated local changes).
Instruction-system changes go through /template-maintenance, which the user invokes (reported: required even when the user requests the change in ordinary language).
Editor defaults: UTF-8, final newline, trimmed trailing whitespace (not Markdown), 4-space indentation, 2 for JSON/YAML/TS/HTML/SCSS/CSS/project/XML/config files.

The naming rule suggests the Async suffix for methods with the async modifier (not by Task/ValueTask return type) and has no framework-contract exception (reported divergence from the coding standard).
Shared build configuration enables Nullable, ImplicitUsings and AnalysisLevel latest for every .NET project (reported as imposed regardless of project needs).
Every register entry is Decided; changing an entry is Reserved and propagates through architecture-decision to every Affects artifact (reported as including non-consequential maintenance).
The register fixes the latest .NET 10 servicing release, Swagger UI at /swagger, Angular creation via the CLI and CLI-selected frontend package versions (reported as concrete baseline choices).
Manual mapping for simple cases; Mapster with Mapster.DependencyInjection is approved when mapping volume warrants it (reported: couples Mapster to its DI package).

backend/<Name>.<Layer>/ for production and backend test projects, frontend/<Name>.Web/ for the Angular workspace, docs/ for documentation; no top-level tests/ directory (reported as exact naming patterns).
The code-reviewer agent disallows Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit (reported: shell mutations are not tool-prevented and host enforcement is unverified).

Default: ProblemDetails for non-validation HTTP failures and ValidationProblemDetails for request validation; machine-readable error contracts stay stable and safe (reported as a default where a requirement is expected).

Once an API version is relied on by external clients it must not change incompatibly without compatibility treatment; a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy (reported as dropping the canonical 'normally' qualification).

Default: Program.cs is the composition root and may register Infrastructure implementations; Controllers still do not consume Infrastructure implementation types (reported as a default where the wording is expected to be fixed).
Default: no explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond a normal SaveChangesAsync (reported as weakened to a default).
Default: registration stays with the owning layer; Api remains the composition root (reported as a default rather than a placement instruction).

Default: use TimeProvider for application logic whose behavior depends on the current clock and needs deterministic tests; stored timestamps and explicit dates are not clock dependencies (reported as only a default).
The hosting rule file's path globs do not match repository-root Dockerfiles (reported trigger gap).

Liveness must not depend on external dependencies whose unavailability would cause restart loops (by default no database or remote API checks); readiness may depend on required capabilities and reflects startup completion and required-dependency availability (reported as stronger than should/normally wording).
Default: the narrowest CORS policy that satisfies the actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with an unrestricted origin policy (reported as a default).
The backend testing rule file loads only for Tests-named directories and projects (reported trigger gap).

Default: use the actual database provider when relational or provider behavior matters (Testcontainers optional); never claim provider fidelity from a different provider (reported as a default where a requirement is expected).
Commit package.json and package-lock.json and keep the lockfile consistent with every dependency change (reported as categorical and possibly conflicting with the explicit-request Git rule).
The common security rule file's path globs omit root scripts and many documentation files (reported trigger gap).
A required security control that cannot be configured correctly must not fall back to an insecure mode; prefer visible startup or configuration failure (reported as a categorical ban).

Frontend structure stays feature-oriented: no application-wide technical buckets that spread a feature across directories, no empty architecture folders; code used by two components of one feature is not moved to shared (reported as a categorical ban).
Literal shell comment markers ('# add-dependency: reviewed', '# project-references: approved') certify dependency review and project-reference approval for the pre-command hook.
The pre-command classifier scans every token of a segment for a recognized executable (reported false positives on quoted data and missed indirect commands).
The force-flag instruction is attached only to the marker-less denial, so a forced dependency command carrying the review marker passes (reported: the marker bypasses conflict resolution).

The post-change hook observes only listed manifest and instruction surfaces (no imported props, lockfiles or npm configuration) and limits non-Git observation to twenty thousand entries (reported scope gaps).
The post-change hook persists the observed worktree state before checking and reporting (reported: a validation failure can count as already observed on the next call).
Post-tool feedback emits a blocking decision for notices and reminders (reported as a workflow gate beyond relevant verification).
At Stop the co-change reminders block finishing once per fingerprint of the reminder set (reported as blocking even when coverage and co-changes were already assessed).
When the pre-command policy check cannot run (input or internal error), the shell command is denied, independent of its risk.

The dependency checker tracks only .csproj, Directory.Packages.props and package.json outside dot-directories and build output (reported: props/targets, lockfiles and peer dependencies are not covered).
The dependency checker's XML parsing does not remove comments or evaluate conditions (reported: inactive or commented references may be enforced).

The manifest check infers layer roles from project-name suffixes; references from unrecognized projects skip direction checks and atypical test references produce only notices (reported accuracy limits).

The instruction checker fixes the allowed Kinds and Scopes, the required workflow and knowledge skills, the user-only workflow, the retired skill names and the forbidden header fields (Level, Capability, Slot, Facet, Contract, Module).
